standard_prerequisites.name: Finite presentation of a module relative to a base ring and its behaviour under localization
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the property being glued and the input that makes the localized modules finitely presented over the localized rings.

standard_prerequisites.name: The cover criterion for finite presentation of a module
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the local finite presentation of the M_{f_i} into finite presentation of M.

standard_prerequisites.name: The auxiliary algebra P = R[x, y, z]/(sum y_i z_i - 1) realizing the cover generators and their unit relation
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the ring over which M becomes a finite module and in which the final vanishing argument is run.

standard_prerequisites.name: A module with vanishing localizations at elements generating the unit ideal is zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the final step closing K/K' = 0.

core_obligations: Deduce the implication (2) => (1) from the localize-relative-finite-presentation lemma (proof lines 21142-21143).

Assume (1), write 1 = sum f_i g_i in A, and choose a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_r, z_1, ..., z_r] -> A mapping y_i to f_i and z_i to g_i, thereby obtaining a surjection P = R[x, y, z]/(sum y_i z_i - 1) -> A with P a finitely presented R-algebra (proof lines 21144-21153).

Use the relatively-finitely-presented lemma to conclude that each M_{f_i} is a finitely presented A_{f_i}-module, hence by the cover criterion that M is a finitely presented A-module, hence a finite P-module (proof lines 21154-21159).
Choose a surjection P^{oplus t} -> M and let K be its kernel; it remains to show K is a finite P-module (proof lines 21160-21161).

Since P_{y_i} surjects onto A_{f_i}, use the cited lemmas to conclude that each localization K_{y_i} is a finitely generated P_{y_i}-module, and choose finitely many elements k_{i,j} of K whose images generate (proof lines 21162-21170).

Let K' be the P-submodule generated by the k_{i,j}; then K/K' has vanishing localization at every y_i, and since the y_i generate the unit ideal of P it follows that K/K' = 0, so K is finite as desired (proof lines 21171-21174).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite type ring map R -> A, an A-module M, and elements f_1, ..., f_r of A generating the unit ideal, and asserts the equivalence of two conditions: that each localization M_{f_i} be finitely presented relative to R, and that M itself be finitely presented relative to R (source lines 21130-21139). One implication is the localize-relative-finite-presentation lemma. For the converse, the proof writes 1 = sum f_i g_i in A and chooses a surjection from a polynomial ring in the x's and two sets of y's and z's onto A mapping y_i to f_i and z_i to g_i; this yields a surjection P = R[x, y, z]/(sum y_i z_i - 1) -> A with P a finitely presented R-algebra (proof lines 21141-21153). By the relatively-finitely-presented lemma each M_{f_i} is a finitely presented A_{f_i}-module, so by the cover criterion M is a finitely presented A-module, hence a finite P-module (proof lines 21154-21159). The substantive part is the verification that the kernel K of a surjection P^{oplus t} -> M is finite: since P_{y_i} surjects onto A_{f_i}, the lemmas cited show that each localization K_{y_i} is a finitely generated P_{y_i}-module; the proof chooses finitely many elements k_{i,j} of K generating all these localizations, lets K' be the P-submodule they generate, and concludes that K/K' has all localizations at the y_i equal to zero, whence K/K' = 0 because the y_i generate the unit ideal of P (proof lines 21160-21174). The non-routine content is the introduction of the auxiliary algebra P, which encodes the cover generators and their unit relation, and the final vanishing argument.
